introduction_markdown: General Certificate of Education (GCE) Board, Ordinary Level, June 2021. Additional Mathematics, Paper 2 (code 0575). Time allowed: two and a half hours. Answer ALL questions in SECTION A (Pure Mathematics, compulsory) and ANY TWO questions from EITHER SECTION B (Mechanics) or SECTION C (Statistics and Probability). In Sections B and C, all questions carry equal marks. Candidates are expected to answer a combination of Section A and Section B OR Section A and Section C, but NOT a combination of all three. If Section B is chosen, Section C may not be chosen, and the other way round. All necessary working must be shown. No marks will be awarded for answers without brief statements showing how the answers have been obtained. Electronic calculators may be used. Where necessary take g as 10 m s^-2. Formulae booklets may be used.
incertitudes: Regles de choix : la consigne imprimee est « Section A obligatoire, puis DEUX questions de la Section B OU DEUX de la Section C, jamais un melange des trois ». Le systeme ne sait exprimer que « 2 parmi 3 » par section ; l'exclusivite B ou C est recopiee dans introduction_markdown mais n'est pas appliquee par les regles_choix.

Points : le sujet imprime des points par sous-question, pas de total par question. Le champ points de chaque exercice est la somme des points imprimes des sous-questions (Section A : 8 ou 9 ; Sections B et C : 17, ce qui est coherent avec « all questions carry equal marks »).

questions.enonce_markdown: (i)(a) The forces $\mathbf F_1=(p\mathbf i+\mathbf j)\,\text N$, $\mathbf F_2=(2q\mathbf i+3p\mathbf j)\,\text N$ and $\mathbf F_3=(\mathbf i+q\mathbf j)\,\text N$ act on a particle of mass $2\,\text{kg}$. Find the resultant of the three forces in terms of $p$ and $q$. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Add the forces component by component:

$\mathbf R=\mathbf F_1+\mathbf F_2+\mathbf F_3=(p+2q+1)\mathbf i+(1+3p+q)\mathbf j.$

**$\mathbf R=\big((p+2q+1)\mathbf i+(3p+q+1)\mathbf j\big)\ \text N$.**
themes: resultant of forces and equilibrium (additional maths)

questions.enonce_markdown: (i)(b) Given that a fourth force $\mathbf F_4=(6\mathbf i)\,\text N$ is added to the system and the system is at equilibrium, find the values of $p$ and $q$. *[5 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
In equilibrium the resultant of all four forces is zero:

$\mathbf R+\mathbf F_4=(p+2q+7)\mathbf i+(3p+q+1)\mathbf j=\mathbf 0.$

Equate each component to zero:

- $p+2q+7=0$ (1)
- $3p+q+1=0$ (2)

From (2): $q=-1-3p$. Substitute in (1): $p+2(-1-3p)+7=0\Rightarrow-5p+5=0\Rightarrow p=1$, hence $q=-1-3=-4$.

Check: $1+2(-4)+7=0$ ✓ and $3(1)+(-4)+1=0$ ✓.

**$p=1,\ q=-4$.** (The mass of the particle is not needed.)
themes: resultant of forces and equilibrium (additional maths)

questions.enonce_markdown: (ii)(a) A car of mass $2000\,\text{kg}$ has a maximum speed of $10\ \text{m s}^{-1}$ up a slope inclined at an angle $\theta$ to the horizontal, where $\sin\theta=0.4$, against a constant resistance of $2000\ \text N$. Find the power generated by the engine of the car. *[4 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
At maximum speed the acceleration is zero, so the driving force $F$ balances the resistance and the component of the weight down the slope:

$F=2000+mg\sin\theta=2000+2000(10)(0.4)=2000+8000=10\,000\ \text N.$

Power $=F\times v=10\,000\times10=100\,000\ \text W.$

**Power $=100\,000\ \text W=100\ \text{kW}$.**
themes: power and resistance of a vehicle

questions.enonce_markdown: (ii)(b) Given that the power generated and the resistance remain unchanged, find the acceleration of the car on a level road at the instant when the speed is $20\ \text{m s}^{-1}$. *[5 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Driving force at $v=20$: $F=\dfrac{P}{v}=\dfrac{100\,000}{20}=5000\ \text N$.

Newton's second law along the level road: $F-R=ma$.

$5000-2000=2000\,a\Rightarrow a=\dfrac{3000}{2000}=1.5.$

**$a=1.5\ \text{m s}^{-2}$.**
themes: power and resistance of a vehicle
